title: How Zero Trust Branch appliance software upgrades run: standalone and HA workflow, the Root FS method and upgrade statuses

prose.text: {{upgrade-available-button}} {{standalone-interruption}} {{ha-staged-order}} {{ha-mixed-versions}} The same page and the HA upgrade page differ on whether the second appliance waits for a test {{divergence:ha-second-upgrade-start}}. The Appliance Version Manager and downgrades are in [[zero-trust-branch.deployment]], and the wider operations area is in [[zero-trust-branch.operations]].

prose.label: Root FS method.
prose.text: {{root-fs-method}} {{root-fs-space}} The Appliance Version Manager page states the Root FS method's status and version range differently {{divergence:root-fs-status-and-versions}}. The mapping between Airgap OS 7.x and 8.x numbering is not in the captured pages {{gap:version-numbering}}.

prose.label: State after the upgrade.
prose.text: {{state-field-values}} {{standalone-active-state}} The standalone upgrade page disagrees with itself on a standalone appliance's state {{divergence:standalone-state-after-upgrade}}. Activation of a hub or spoke is in [[zero-trust-branch.operations.routed-tunnels]].

upgrade-available-button.statement: The Sites page in the Zscaler Admin Console shows an Upgrade available button to indicate that a site is eligible for upgrade.

quotes: A rich set of upgrade options are available from the Sites page in the Zscaler Admin Console. An Upgrade available button indicates that a site is eligible for upgrade.

standalone-interruption.statement: Upgrading a standalone appliance briefly interrupts traffic forwarding while it reboots, with no failover because there is no secondary appliance.

quotes: Traffic forwarding is briefly interrupted while the appliance reboots (no failover occurs, as there is no secondary appliance).

ha-staged-order.statement: In an HA pair the standby appliance B is upgraded first and becomes Active, then appliance A is upgraded, and both remain in their new Active and Standby states.

quotes: Appliance B (Standby) is upgraded first.
After the upgrade, appliance B becomes Active and starts handling traffic.
Appliance A (originally Active and now Standby) is upgraded.
the appliances remain in their new Active and Standby states.

ha-mixed-versions.statement: For versions 8.0.7 or later HA appliances need not run the same version, so one can be upgraded and tested first, and an appliance can be reverted to the old version if errors occur after upgrading.

quotes: For versions 8.0.7 or later, appliances need not run the same version.
If any errors or issues occur with the appliance after upgrading to a new version, you can revert to the old version.
You can upgrade one appliance first and test it for performance and stability before upgrading the other appliance.

root-fs-method.statement: The Root FS upgrade method (currently in Preview) downloads up to three image versions, lets one be designated the default so it is applied automatically during a factory reset, and supports only appliances with versions 8.0.6 or later.

quotes: The Root FS upgrade method allows you to download up to three image versions of the Zero Trust Branch appliance software
You can also designate one version as a default version, which allows Zero Trust Branch to apply the image automatically during a factory reset.
This upgrade method is currently in Preview.
Only Zero Trust Branch appliances with versions 8.0.6 or later are supported.

root-fs-space.statement: From version 8.0.6 the image size was optimized to store up to three images, but if older images such as 8.0.4 HF1 are present the download or installation of the third image might fail for lack of space, which deleting an older image avoids.

quotes: Beginning with version 8.0.6 and later, the image size was optimized to allow downloading and storing up to three images on the appliance.
If your appliance includes older images (e.g., 8.0.4 HF1), the downloading and installation of the third image might fail due to space constraints.
To avoid this issue, you can delete one of the older images.

ha-upgrade-statuses.statement: During an HA upgrade the appliance status moves through Downloading, Updating, Restarting, Initializing and Post-Update to Active or Standby; after one appliance completes it becomes Active, the other goes to Standby, and its upgrade starts automatically using the method of the previous appliance.

quotes: Downloading | The Zero Trust Branch appliance software version is being downloaded.
Updating | The downloaded version is being applied to the Zero Trust Branch appliance.
Restarting | The Zero Trust Branch appliance is rebooting after the update.
Initializing | The Zero Trust Branch appliance is initializing with the new software version.
Post-Update | The Zero Trust Branch appliance is running the necessary scripts, utilities, and containers.
Active or Standby | The update is completed and the Zero Trust Branch appliance has resumed normal operation.

After completing the upgrade process, the Zero Trust Branch appliance automatically transitions to the Active state. The other Zero Trust Branch appliance goes to the Standby state, and the upgrade process starts automatically based on the method used for the previous Zero Trust Branch appliance.

standalone-upgrade-statuses.statement: During a standalone upgrade the status moves through Downloading, Updating, Restarting, Initializing and Post-Update to Standalone when the update is completed.

quotes: Downloading | The Zero Trust Branch appliance software version is being downloaded.
Updating | The downloaded version is being applied to the Zero Trust Branch appliance.
Restarting | The Zero Trust Branch appliance is rebooting after the update.
Initializing | The Zero Trust Branch appliance is initializing with the new software version.
Post-Update | The Zero Trust Branch appliance is running the necessary scripts, utilities, and containers.
Standalone | The update is completed and the Zero Trust Branch appliance has resumed normal operation.

standalone-active-state.statement: The standalone upgrade page says that after the upgrade the appliance automatically transitions to the Active state.

quotes: After completing the upgrade process, the Zero Trust Branch appliance automatically transitions to the Active state.

state-field-values.statement: The site-details State field of an activated appliance is Standalone for a standalone appliance, Active for the primary node of an HA cluster and Standby for the secondary node.

quotes: Standalone for a standalone appliance
Active for the primary node of an HA cluster
Standby for the secondary node of an HA cluster
The State field value for an activated appliance is:
In the site details, verify that the appliance is activated.

standalone-state-after-upgrade.summary: The standalone upgrade page says the appliance transitions to the Active state after the upgrade, while its status table ends in Standalone.

positions.says: After a standalone upgrade the appliance automatically transitions to the Active state.

quotes: After completing the upgrade process, the Zero Trust Branch appliance automatically transitions to the Active state.

positions.says: After a standalone upgrade the status is Standalone once the update is completed.

quotes: Standalone | The update is completed and the Zero Trust Branch appliance has resumed normal operation.

standalone-state-after-upgrade.impact: An admin watching a standalone appliance after an upgrade may expect Active or Standalone; the Standalone status matches the State field values recorded for activated appliances.

root-fs-status-and-versions.summary: The standalone upgrade page calls the Root FS method Preview and supports versions 8.0.6 or later, while the Appliance Version Manager page treats it as a supported method from 8.0.7 and the only method from 8.1.1.

positions.says: The Root FS upgrade method is currently in Preview and supports only appliances with versions 8.0.6 or later.

quotes: This upgrade method is currently in Preview.
Only Zero Trust Branch appliances with versions 8.0.6 or later are supported.

positions.says: Both legacy and Root FS-based methods are supported on 8.0.7 or later, and from 8.1.1 only the Root FS-based method is supported.

quotes: Zero Trust Branch supports both legacy and Root FS-based Appliance Version Manager methods for upgrading appliances running version 8.0.7 or later.
Starting with version 8.1.1, you can upgrade using only the Root FS-based Appliance Version Manager, as the legacy method is no longer supported.

positions.says: The Appliance Version Manager stores up to three image versions (8.0.7 or later).

quotes: allows you to download and store up to three Zero Trust Branch image versions (8.0.7 or later).

root-fs-status-and-versions.impact: The pages give 8.0.6 and 8.0.7 as the first Root FS release and disagree on whether it is Preview or the sole method from 8.1.1; check the page for the appliance's version before relying on Root FS.

ha-second-upgrade-start.summary: The software upgrades page lets an HA pair run different versions so one appliance can be upgraded and tested first, while the HA upgrade page says the second appliance's upgrade starts automatically.

positions.says: One appliance can be upgraded and tested for performance and stability before the other.

quotes: You can upgrade one appliance first and test it for performance and stability before upgrading the other appliance.

positions.says: After the first appliance completes, the other goes to Standby and its upgrade starts automatically.

quotes: The other Zero Trust Branch appliance goes to the Standby state, and the upgrade process starts automatically based on the method used for the previous Zero Trust Branch appliance.

ha-second-upgrade-start.impact: Whether the second HA appliance can be held back for testing is unsettled; the first page ties this to versions 8.0.7 or later and the second does not state a version.

version-numbering.title: How the Airgap OS 7.x version numbers map to the 8.x release numbers
version-numbering.detail: The captured Root FS and upgrade pages give version numbers (8.0.6, 8.0.7) and other Zero Trust Branch pages give Airgap OS 7.7.6 and 7.7.x, but no captured page maps the two numbering schemes.
